sentences.text:
The case of the Petitioner in brief is as follows:-
On 03.07.2022 at about 3.00pm the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in the TVS Victor motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-11-Q-6831, the said motorcycle was being ridden by her father on the extreme left side of the Road near S.C.Circle,
Hirisave Village, Channarayanapatna Taluk, Hassan District, a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MK-1329 came with high speed driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life, all of a sudden came to wrong/right side of the Road from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately she was shifted to Punya Hospital,
Channarayapatna and admitted and treated as an inpatient from 03.07.2022 to 07.07.2022, surgery was done and discharged with advice to take complete bed rest.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Before the accident she was hale and healthy and was studying 5th Std.

Due to the accidental fracture of left hand and disability she is unable to attend her class and also unable to do any physical strain work,
from this disability which affected the present and future life.

The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MK-1329 and the Hirisave Police have registered a case against the Driver of the Car in Cr.No.94/2022.
Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence this petition.
4. In spite of due service of summons, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

Darshini .D.K vs Gopalashetty M.V on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143839507/
2

5. The objections of the Respondent No.1 is that, He has denied all the petition averments except admitting that the Car was insured with the 2 nd respondent and the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
He has denied the manner of accident.
The accident caused due to the sole negligence of the rider of the TVS XL who is the father of the petitioner.
He has denied the accidental injuries to the petitioner, medical expenses.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. The objections of the Respondent No.2 is that, It has denied all the petition averments.
It has denied issuing the policy to the Car bearing No.KA-02-MK-1329 pending confirmation from the concerned branch.
There is non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
The Driver of the Car did not have valid DL as on the date of accident.

Further stated that the accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner's father i.e., the rider of the TVS XL motorcycle and the rider of the said vehicle did not possess valid DL as on the date of accident.
The minor petitioner did not wear helmet at the time of accident.

Further it has denied the age, manner of accident, injuries suffered by the petitioner, medical expenses etc., and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1 Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident took place on 03.07.2022 at about 3.00pm near SC Circle, Hirisave Village, Channrayapatna Taluk, Hassan District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MK-1329 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom payable?
3.
What order or award?
8. The Father/natural guardian of the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 9.
Dr.Mahesh V got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.10 to P.13.
On the other side, the Respondents have not examined any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
9. Heard the arguments on both sides.

10. On hearing both sides and perusal of evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Case No. Issue No.1 Issue No.2 Issue No.3 In the As per the MVC 4525/2022 Affirmative In the Affirmative Final order REASONS 11. Issue No.1:
Darshini .D.K vs Gopalashetty M.V on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143839507/
3
In order to prove the negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MK-1329, the Petitioner got examined her father/next friend as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 5.
He has reiterated the petitioner averments in his examination in chief.
During the cross examination of PW.1, he has stated that the accident was a head on collision.
The Respondent No.2 has contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The accident caused due to the negligence of the petitioner's father/rider of the motorcycle.
12. On perusal of Ex.P.1 it is clear that the FIR was registered on the same day of the accident on the complaint of father of the Petitioner.
Ex. P.2
Crime Details Form/IMV report and the spot mahazar was conducted on 07.07.2022 at about 9.30 to 10.15am.
The sketch at Ex.P.3 shows that the accident occurred in the middle of the Shravanabelagola Main Road.
The vehicle seizure mahazar was conducted on 07.07.2022 at about 12.00 to 1.00pm.
The Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the Car after thorough investigation as per Ex.P.5.
The respondents have not produced any documents to show the negligence of the father of the petitioner.
Therefore, on the basis of all these documents, this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MK-1329.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is held in affirmative.
13. Issue No.2
In order to prove her disability the petitioner got marked Ex.P.6 Discharge Summary of Punya Hospital.
As per Ex.P.6 the petitioner has suffered pain, swelling, deformity and ROM- REN of left Forearm.

14. The Petitioner, in order to show that she has suffered these disabilities, has got examined Dr.Mahesh V. as PW.2, he has deposed that the petitioner has suffered Pain/Swelling deformity left Forearm.
X-ray shows fracture left Radius and Ulna.
The petitioner got operated with plates and screws for radius and Tens for Ulna.

He got marked Exs.P.10 to P.13, copy of MLC register extract,
police intimation, case sheet and 2 old X-rays and one new X-ray.
PW.2 has assessed the total loss of percentage of disability for left upper limb at 31%.

Disability:
15.
During the cross examination of PW.2, he has stated that he has treated the petitioner and she was an inpatient for 4 days.
The petitioner was stable at the time of discharge.
It takes around 5 months for complete union of fracture.
The fracture is mal-united.
On perusal of the evidence of PW.2 it is clear that the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries.
The injuries to the left Forearm has caused restricted left wrist and forearm movements with pain/swelling with implants in situ and having difficulty in lifting and carrying the weight.
As such, she lost her Academics and unable to take care of herself.
However, the petitioner is young and she has to suffer the disability through out her life.
Therefore, on the basis of the evidence of Pw.2, this tribunal deems it fit to fix the whole body disability at 11%.

sentences.text: The Petitioner, in order to prove her age, has produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.7.
As per the said document, her date of birth is 09.07.2012.
The accident occurred on 03.07.2022.
As such, as on the date of accident the age of the Petitioner is considered as 10 years.
Quantum of Income and quantum of compensation 17.
The Petitioner, as on the date of accident, admittedly was a minor.
Therefore, she was not earning anything.

As per the decision of Hon'ble supreme court reported in ILR 2014 Kar 4891 rendered in Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance having regard to relevant factors, precedents and approach of various Hon'ble High Courts with regard to the compensation of the child victims, held that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc., should be Rs.1,00,000/- disability up to 10%, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to whole body 3 lakhs: up to 60% 4 lakhs: up to 90% 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance

sentences.text: In the present case the Petitioner is suffering from disability to the tune of 11% and she was hospitalized for about 4 days as could be made out from Ex.P.6 discharge summary of Punya Hospital.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head of pain and suffering already undergone including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.

18. The Petitioner was inpatient from 03.07.202 to 07.07.2022, diagnosed and treated to the pain,
swelling, deformity of left forearm and discharged with follow up treatment.
This must have caused loss of some income and discomforts to the parents of the Petitioner during that period.

Therefore,
his parents are entitled for a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the heads of loss of income and discomforts to the parents.
The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that he has spent considerable amount towards her conveyance and nourishment etc.,
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
The PW.1 stated that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
In this regard the Petitioner has produced 19 medical bills as per Ex.P.8 for a sum of Rs.64,351/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.64,351/- under the heads of medical expenses.
PW.2 has stated that the petitioner is in need of one more surgery for removal of implants which cost about Rs.20,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 did not produce any estimation bill or any other documents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards Future Medical Expenses.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-
Sl. HEAD COMPENSATION No. AMOUNT 1. Pain and suffering already Rs.3,00,000/-
 undergone and to be suffered in  future including loss of comforts  amenities on account of  disability.

2. Discomforts, inconvenience and Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of earnings of the parent  during the laid up period.

5 3.

Medical Bills Rs.64,351/-
4. Conveyance, attendant and Rs.20,000/-
 nourishment etc.

5. Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.4,44,351/-
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.4,44,500/- and the same is awarded to the petitioner under different heads.
LIABILITY 19.
The Respondents did not prove their defence.
Therefore, the Respondents being the Owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Insurance policy is proved to be in force by the Petitioner, the Respondent No.2 insurer has primary liability to satisfy the award.
Though the petitioner has claimed Rs.10,00,000/- compensation.
But the petitioner is entitled to Rs.4,44,351/- along with interest @ 6% pa.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 held in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.3 :

In view of above answers to issue Nos.1 & 2, this court proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is hereby allowed with cost.
The Respondents 1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,44,351/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Forty Four Thousand and Three Hundred and Fifty One only) along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

On deposit of compensation and interest, Rs.1,00,000/- shall be released in favour of the guardian of the Petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules and remaining amount shall deposited in the name of the minor petitioner till she attains the age of majority in any Bank.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
